Krichene and Rendle show that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model orderings relative to full-catalog evaluation—even in expectation; smaller candidate samples also blur differences between ranking metrics. Thus, HR@10 against 99 negatives supports claims about that sampled benchmark, without establishing full-catalog superiority. Fixing users, negatives and evaluation seed enables controlled comparisons but does not eliminate sampling bias. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged and state its candidate protocol explicitly. [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For uncertainty analysis, a suitable application of paired bootstrap resampling is to retain both models’ per-user hit indicators, resample the same user indices for both models within each category, then recompute the equally weighted four-category mean difference. Report the observed difference and bootstrap confidence interval; pairing preserves within-user dependence. With 200 users per category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and the macro-average by 0.00125. Such intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed candidates and trained models; they exclude training-seed and negative-sampling variation. [Bootstrap resampling methodology](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/)

Repeatedly selecting architectures or checkpoints on the same validation users can overfit the selection criterion. Ordinary bootstrap intervals computed after adaptive search do not remove this selection bias. Record trial counts and selection rules, label validation gains exploratory, and reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation. Full-catalog simulator recommendations are a separate operating setting, so sampled validation gains alone cannot establish their quality. [Cawley and Talbot, 2010](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
